lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # GLOSSARY.md Format

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: `GLOSSARY.md` is the canonical language for this teaching workspace. All explainers, exercises, and learning records should adhere to its terminology. Building it is itself part of learning: compressing a concept into a tight definition is evidence the user understands it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Structure

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```md

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # {Topic} Glossary

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: {One or two sentence description of the topic this glossary covers.}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Terms

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Hypertrophy**:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Muscle growth driven by mechanical tension and metabolic stress over repeated training sessions.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: _Avoid_: Bulking, getting big

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Progressive overload**:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Systematically increasing the demand on a muscle over time — via load, volume, or intensity.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: _Avoid_: Pushing harder, levelling up

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion)**:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A 1–10 self-rating of how hard a set felt, where 10 is failure and 8 means two reps left in the tank.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: _Avoid_: Effort score, intensity rating

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Rules

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Add a term only when the user understands it.** The glossary is a record of compressed knowledge, not a dictionary the user reads to learn. If the user has just been introduced to a concept, wait until they can use it correctly before promoting it here.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Be opinionated.** When several words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the rest as aliases to avoid. This is how language compresses.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences. Define what the term IS, not what it does or how to do it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Use the glossary's own terms inside definitions.** Once a term is in the glossary, prefer it everywhere — including inside other definitions. This is what makes complex terms easier to grasp later.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Group under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge (e.g. `## Anatomy`, `## Programming`). A flat list is fine when terms cohere.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Flag ambiguities explicitly.** If a term is used loosely in the wider field, note the resolution: "In this workspace, 'set' always means a working set — warm-ups are tracked separately."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Revise as understanding deepens.** A definition the user wrote in week one may be wrong by week six. Update in place; do not leave stale entries.
